newsitem.title: USA: State Department says summit talks to take place.
newsitem.headline: State Department says summit talks to take place.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Monday it expects Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to attend Middle East summit talks in Washington on Tuesday and Wednesday.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told CNN: "I think the summit leaders will be here this week." He was responding to questions on Arafat's reported request for a delay in the talks called by President Bill Clinton.
"We expect to have meetings on Tuesday and Wednesday" as scheduled, Burns said.
"I expect he will be here," Burns said, adding that U.S. officials have been involved in around-the-clock discussions with PLO leaders about the peace talks.
Arafat has asked Clinton to delay the proposed summit in Washington with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu until differences over the agenda were settled, PLO officials have said.
Burns echoed earlier comments by State Department Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross on NBC television's "Today" program.
